top_story_title: A KEV-listed Brotli flaw reaches Cisco products through Node.js (CVE-2026-111497)
top_story_summary: Node.js published fixes on 21 October 2026 across its 22.x, 24.x and 26.x release lines, and Cisco's October PSIRT advisory confirms that four of those issues affect Cisco products with a Security Impact Rating of High: CVE-2026-111497 (Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write, potential remote code execution), CVE-2026-105482 (DNS resolution truncation involving embedded NUL characters), CVE-2026-105483 (TLS hostname validation bypass using fullwidth IP digits) and CVE-2026-106069 (TLS hostname validation bypass with noncanonical IP addresses).
top_actions: Pull the affected-products table from the Cisco advisory and match it against your asset inventory by product and running version; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release, as none is stated in the feed text.

Prioritise CVE-2026-111497: it is on the CISA KEV catalog (added 2026-10-27, BOD 26-04 due 2026-11-10, now overdue). Federal operators must patch or discontinue use of the product; everyone else should treat it as confirmed-exploited and schedule an emergency change.

Where no fixed release exists yet for a product you run, cut exposure now: management HTTPS/SSH/API off any untrusted or internet-facing interface, restricted to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network, with MFA on every admin account.

Because CVE-2026-105483 and CVE-2026-106069 bypass TLS hostname validation, review the connections your devices make outbound - licensing, telemetry, cloud management, syslog over TLS - and confirm certificate pinning or an explicit trust list where the platform supports it.
Ship device and management-platform logs to the SIEM and alert on admin logins, configuration changes and software/firmware changes for the duration of the patch cycle.
executive_summary: Cisco's October Node.js advisory carries CVE-2026-111497, a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write already on CISA's KEV catalog (added 2026-10-27, BOD 26-04 due 2026-11-10, now overdue) - emergency change for any affected Cisco product.

Two TLS hostname-validation bypasses in the same advisory (CVE-2026-105483, CVE-2026-106069) weaken the trust decisions a device makes on connections it initiates, not inbound access - review pinning on licensing, telemetry and cloud-management links.

Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938, CVSS 4.0 9.2) is unauthenticated RCE in the OpenJDK Base64 decoder on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI, fixed 17 November 2026; inventory the Java runtimes sitting under network management, NAC and identity servers. Check Point says IPS coverage for the public PoC is live, but that is cover while you patch, not a fix.
No source in this window states a fixed release for a Cisco product - verify every version number in the vendor advisory before you book a change window.
Thin cycle otherwise: 9 items reached the digest, 5 dropped as outside network infrastructure (threat-actor reporting, SaaS outage posts, scam psychology, distro patching process).
key_actions: **Cisco** — Identify affected devices from your asset inventory filtered by Cisco product and running version, using the advisory's affected-products table; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release rather than assuming a build.

**Cisco** — Patch CVE-2026-111497 on an emergency change: KEV-listed, unauthenticated, remote-code-execution potential, and already past its BOD 26-04 due date of 2026-11-10. Federal operators must patch or discontinue use of the product.

ai_defenses.solution: Security framework for the agentic enterprise
ai_defenses.what_it_does: A Cisco Fellow sets out why concrete, vendor-neutral security architectures are needed for AI agents and works through a technical example. It is a documented architectural approach, not a product.

headlines.title: Vulnerabilities in Node.js and Brotli Affecting Cisco Products: October 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco's October Node.js advisory covers four high-severity flaws in Cisco products, led by the KEV-listed Brotli decoder bug CVE-2026-111497 that can reach remote code execution.

headlines.title: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938): Check Your Java Services Now
headlines.summary: Check Point says IPS protection for the public Java4Shell proof-of-concept is live on its gateways, with fixes for CVE-2026-114938 released 17 November 2026.

headlines.title: CVE-2026-114938: Critical vulnerability in OpenJDK Java
headlines.summary: Cisco Talos is tracking Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a CVSS 4.0 9.2 OpenJDK flaw that may give unauthenticated remote code execution to anything exposing a Java runtime.

headlines.title: Building a Security Framework for the Agentic Enterprise
headlines.summary: Cisco makes the case for concrete, vendor-neutral security architectures for AI agents and publishes a technical example, with no product attached.
